reason: The goal says to arrange the mirror strips around the triangular former, so I’ll start there.
expectation: I expect the strips to form a triangular mirror assembly, though I’m not sure whether they’ll be secured yet.

alternatives.reason: The coloured shapes also look useful, but the current goal points to the mirrors first.

effect: The mirrors form a triangle, and their repeated reflections can enlarge a small view into a pattern. Next I need to secure them.
reaction: I’m curious to see what pattern the mirrors make.
reason: The current goal says to tape the mirror triangle together.
expectation: I expect the tape to hold the three mirrors in their triangular arrangement.

alternatives.reason: Preparing the coloured shapes seems useful later, but the goal points to securing the mirrors first.

effect: The mirror triangle is bound, so it is ready to go into the tube.
reason: The goal directs me to slide the mirror triangle into the viewing tube.
expectation: I expect the outer tube to enclose and protect the mirrors.

alternatives.reason: The colour cell looks useful, but I’ll follow the current construction step first.

effect: The mirror triangle is inside a tube with an eyepiece; the next goal is to prepare the colour cell.
reason: The goal calls for putting the coloured pieces in their cell, and this is the only combination offered.
expectation: I expect the coloured shapes to be enclosed in the clear cell, ready to attach to the mirror tube.

effect: The shapes are loose inside the closed drum so they can slide and change the pattern; it is ready to fit to the tube.
reaction: Leaving space for the shapes makes physical sense.
reason: The goal says to fit the colour cell to the viewing tube, and this is the only combination offered.
expectation: I expect the drum to attach to the tube so the mirrors can reflect the coloured shapes.

effect: The rotating colour drum is attached to the mirror tube; the next step is to cover the cell.
reason: The goal specifies the light cover, and this is the only combination offered.
expectation: I expect the cover to fit over the drum and diffuse light entering the colour cell.

effect: The cover is fitted, and the kaleidoscope is ready to be tested with light.
reaction: I’m curious to see the changing pattern.
reason: The goal says to hold it toward the lantern and turn it; this is the only combination offered.
expectation: I expect the lantern to illuminate the coloured shapes and reveal changing reflected patterns as the drum turns.

effect: The lantern test showed how the mirrors multiply the coloured shapes and how turning the drum changes the pattern. The chapter is complete.
reaction: The tumbling pattern and Jo’s unusually quiet reaction were satisfying.

mostWorthwhile.text: Testing the finished kaleidoscope was most worthwhile: the small collection of shapes became a changing crowd of colours.

leastWorthwhile.text: Taping and enclosing the mirrors felt straightforward but less interesting than seeing them work.

surprise.text: I liked learning that the shapes need room to slide so the pattern can change.

arbitrary.text: No action felt arbitrary; the goals gave each fitting a clear construction purpose, though several were the only offered combination.

continue.text: Yes, I would try another chapter to see another mechanism come together; the final kaleidoscope made the guided assembly worthwhile.
